cells.tense: Right now you can sit with someone's distress without being pulled under it.
cells.act: hold the weight as a builder holds stone
cells.ask: Stay with what someone is feeling, without reaching to fix it, and hold it steady the way stone carries weight.
cells.core: You can be with what people feel without going under. In the live mix, your care works like a vessel rather than a current: you notice what to add, what to subtract, how to blend, and you don't have to match the feeling to stay near it. Someone can be in pieces beside you and still have someone to lean on. That steadiness is a real thing you do. It is free to feed something sturdier in you now — care with weight to it, that holds a shape and doesn't dissolve on contact. Hold like stone holds: unmoved, containing, not crushing. Staying when leaving would be easier counts more than you tend to give it credit for.
cells.sheetLine: You can stay with someone's feeling without going under.
cells.verb: Tend the space between people, holding feeling without tightening around it.
cells.place: The live mix — sensing what to add, what to subtract, how to blend, moment by moment.

cells.tense: Soon you will be bracing for a future you can't write in, and reaching has turned into gripping.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Set down one thread you keep holding for someone just in case, and don't watch what happens next.
cells.core: Out on the growing edge, you're bracing for something that hasn't arrived, and your reach has become gripping. You keep space ready for feelings that may not come, hold every thread loose in case it's needed, adjust for a room that isn't here. From outside it looks like constant readiness. From inside it feels like care, but it's heavier than care. What's truly done can be recognised as done, and what still serves can stay without being guarded. You can set down something you've been carrying for someone's future, and feel where providing ends and over-providing begins. Putting it down now doesn't make you careless — the care stays, lighter and more accurate, pointed at what's actually here.

cells.tense: You were the one who could hold it, and you haven't stepped into the room since it changed.
cells.act: hold the clarity steady and tempered
cells.ask: Offer one blunt, kind observation about what you see right now and don't retract it.
cells.core: In the live mix, you're playing the old part while the music has changed. Your sense of what to add and what to subtract runs on memory — how you used to blend, what used to land — and little of it reaches now. The gap shows as hanging back: you attend from the edge rather than inside the moment, and the room stops feeling like one you're part of. Pushing feeling into a starved place fills nothing. What moves things is clear words brought to where you actually stand. Say one plain thing you notice, hold it steady, and don't retract it. You don't have to manufacture warmth you don't feel yet. The words said once start the current again, and the room you left can stay left.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you're already writing in, and you'd call it just listening.
cells.act: cut to the logic and act on it
cells.ask: Name the pattern inside one stuck situation, then move on it — no rehearsal, no second opinion.
cells.core: You've been tuning the room — a little more here, a little less there, keeping the whole thing steady — and those adjustments are real. They steer what happens next, and your own account has you merely listening. The hand on them isn't yours in the story you tell. Feeling more won't fix that; seeing more sharply will. There's a pattern sitting inside whatever keeps recurring, and you can find it by stopping mid-adjustment and working it through plainly. Cut to the logic of one stuck moment, and act from what you find. Not a theory of yourself — just one clear read, and one move taken from it. That puts your hand back on the page you were already writing.
